323939.title: The near-field conjecture for sharply 2-transitive groups
323939.literal_statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a sharply $2$-transitive permutation group, meaning that it acts transitively and freely on ordered pairs of distinct points. A **near field** is a skew field that is distributive only from the left. **Near-field conjecture.** There exists a near field $N$ such that

$$
\Gamma=N^{\times}\ltimes N.
$$

This conjecture characterizes sharply $2$-transitive groups as the affine groups of near fields. It was confirmed for finite sharply $2$-transitive groups by H. Zassenhaus in 1936, and the paper proves it for the linear groups under the stated hypotheses.

323958.title: The conjecture for binomials x^{q-2}+t x^{q^2-q-1}
323958.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let $t\in\Bbb F_q^*$. Define

$$
f(x)=x^{q-2}+t x^{q^2-q-1}.
$$

**The conjecture for binomials $x^{q-2}+t x^{q^2-q-1}$.** The polynomial $f$ is a permutation polynomial of $\Bbb F_{q^2}$ if and only if one of the following holds: (i) $t=1$ and $q\equiv 1\pmod 4$; (ii) $t=-3$ and $q\equiv\pm1\pmod{12}$; or (iii) $t=3$ and $q\equiv-1\pmod 6$. This conjecture arose from the preceding theorem and a computer search of the remaining cases, and it aims to classify the permutation behavior of this binomial over $\Bbb F_{q^2}$.

325332.literal_statement:

op_{[2^{k+2}]}(123)= \frac{329k^3+1215k^2+1426k+528}{2(k+2)(2k+5)(7k+5)}op_{[2^{k+1}]}(123)+\frac{3(k+1)(2k+1)(7k+12)}{(k+2)(2k+5)(7k+5)}op_{[2^k]}(123).

329435.title: The q-analogue identity for rook placements and the Harer–Zagier formula
329435.literal_statement:
Let $Y(n,s)$ be the set of all Young diagrams with $n$ rows of lengths between $s$ and $n+s$. For a rook placement $C$ on a diagram $[?]$ in $Y(n,s)$, let $\operatorname{inv}(C)$ be the number of blank squares left after crossing out every square directly to the left of or above a rook, let $|\mu|$ denote the number of squares of $\mu$, and write $[m]_q$ for the $q$-integer, $[m]_q!!$ for the corresponding $q$-double factorial, and $\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{a}{b}_q$ for the $q$-binomial coefficient. **The q-analogue conjecture.** The following identity holds:

$$
\sum_{\mu \in Y(n,s)} \prod_{i=1}^{n}q^{\mu_i-i}[\mu_i-i+1]_q = \sum_{\mu \in Y(n,s)}\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{rook placements}\\ C \,\operatorname{on}\, \mu}}q^{\operatorname{inv}(C) + |\mu| - \binom{n+1}{2}}
$$

$$
=\sum_{k\geq 0} q^{n(s-k) + \binom{k}{2}}[2n-1]_q!!\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{s}{k}_q\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{k}_q\prod_{i=1}^k(1 + q^{n+i}).
$$

This gives a $q$-analogue of the rook-placement expression for the Harer–Zagier formula; it was verified computationally up to $n=10$ and $s=5$, but no proof or general resolution is supplied in the source.

335361.title: Carpenter–Tonchev rank conjecture for designs from maximal arcs
335361.literal_statement:
Let $t\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a $2-(2^{2t-1}-2^{t-1},2^{t-1},1)$ design with incidence matrix $A$. **Carpenter–Tonchev's rank conjecture.** The binary rank of $A$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{rank}_{2}(A)\geq 3^t-2^t,
$$

and equality

$$
\operatorname{rank}_{2}(A)=3^t-2^t
$$

holds if and only if $\mathcal{D}$ is embeddable as a maximal $(2^{2t-1}-2^{t-1},2^{t-1})$-arc in $PG(2^t,2)$. This strengthens a conjecture attributed to Laurel Carpenter that the binary rank of every design associated with a hyperoval in $PG(2,2^t)$ equals $3^t-2^t$, and generalizes a conjecture of A. E. Brouwer. The computations in the paper support the conjecture for the 93 designs arising from hyperovals in $PG(2,16)$, but the general assertion remains open.

341975.title: Gallai-Ramsey number conjecture for the three-triangle fan
341975.literal_statement:
Let $F_n$ be the fan graph with $n$ triangles, defined by

$$
F_n=K_1+n\overline{K_2},
$$

$$

14\cdot 5^{\frac{k-2}{2}}-1, & \text{if }k\text{ is even};\\
33\cdot 5^{\frac{k-3}{2}}, & \text{if }k\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

344050.title: Cyclic reciprocal squared-difference conjecture for permutations
344050.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$ be a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. **Cyclic squared-difference conjecture.** If $n>11$, there is a permutation $\pi$ such that

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{1}{\pi(k)^2-\pi(k+1)^2}+\frac{1}{\pi(n)^2-\pi(1)^2}=0.
$$

The paper introduces this as a further conjecture motivated by the preceding non-cyclic squared-difference conjecture, and explicitly distinguishes it from the conjectures of Sun it has just reproduced.

344499.title: Brualdi–Stein conjecture on near transversals in Latin squares
344499.literal_statement:
A **Latin square** is an $n\times n$ array in which each symbol occurs exactly once in every row and column. A **near transversal** is a partial transversal of length $n-1$, meaning a set of $n-1$ entries chosen from distinct rows and columns with distinct symbols.

**Brualdi–Stein conjecture.** Every Latin square contains a near transversal.

This conjecture is attributed to Brualdi and Stein, and in another source to Ryser. It has been proved for Cayley tables of finite groups and for Latin squares of order at most $11$, but remains open in general.

382072.title: The Ramanujan–Kolberg identity conjecture for multipartitions
382072.literal_statement:
Let $p_t(n)$ denote the number of $t$-multipartitions of $n$. Let $a$ and $t$ be odd integers, with $3\mid t$ whenever $3\mid a$. Define $b$ by

$$
b\equiv \frac{t}{3}\cdot 8^{-1}
$$

when $3\mid t$, and by $b\equiv24^{-1}\pmod a$ otherwise, and set

$$
k=\left\lceil\frac{t(a^2-1)}{24a}\right\rceil.
$$

Here $f_d$ denotes the standard eta-product factor used in the source, and $\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}$ are coefficients in $\{0,1\}$. **Ramanujan–Kolberg identity conjecture.** There is a suitable choice of the $\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}$ such that $\epsilon^t_{a,1,0}=1$, $\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}=0$ whenever $at/d-24j<0$, and

$$
q^k\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_t(an+b)q^n\equiv\sum_{d\mid a}\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor k/d\rfloor}\frac{\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}q^{dj}}{f_d^{at/d-24j}}.
$$

The conjecture predicts that these subprogression generating functions lie in a particularly structured, relatively low-dimensional space of modular forms. The supplied text says Chen proved it for, among other cases, all primes $a\geq3$, so the general conjecture remains open.
